description:
FILED s1061 (Opus, 2026-09-07), found behind #1505 while bisecting #1061's CPAN-board down-movers.

perl's `import Foo LIST;` is a plain method call `Foo->import(LIST)` whenever
`import` is not a sub in scope.  PCL special-cases only the ARGUMENT-LESS
two-Word shape (`import Foo;`, Pl/Parser.pm's `@parts == 2` branch, which
#1505 just corrected); with an argument list the statement falls through to
the ordinary expression path, where the package NAME is parsed as a function
call:

    import constant HAVE_THREADS => 0;
      ->  (p-void-ctx (pl-import (p-list-ctx (pl-constant "HAVE_THREADS" 0))))
      ->  "Undefined subroutine &main::constant called"

REPRODUCER (perl prints "imported: A=1"; PCL dies):

    package My::Mod;
    sub import { my $c = shift; print "imported: @_\n" }
    package main;
    BEGIN { $INC{'My/Mod.pm'} = 1; require My::Mod; import My::Mod A => 1; }

WHERE IT COSTS ROWS.  Scalar-List-Utils t/dualvar.t (CPAN board) has

    BEGIN {
      if ($Config{'useithreads'}) { require threads; import threads;
                                    require threads::shared; import threads::shared;
                                    require constant; import constant HAVE_THREADS => 1; }
      else                        { require constant; import constant HAVE_THREADS => 0; }
    }

With #1505 in, the file READS again but its BEGIN now dies here, so the row
stays FAIL 0/0 where perl gives 41/0 and PCL gave 14/2 before s436's phase
model moved the BEGIN ahead of the assertions.

TWO THINGS TO SETTLE BEFORE FIXING (do not just widen the branch):
  1. `constant->import(...)` needs somewhere to land.  PCL has NO
     `lib/constant.pm` -- `use constant` is compile-time special-cased into a
     `defconstant`.  A run-time `import constant NAME => VALUE` therefore
     needs either a shim or a runtime entry point.  That is a LAYER decision
     (CLAUDE.md 9a): `constant` is a core pragma, so a `lib/constant.pm`
     shim whose `import` installs the sub is the shape that matches every
     other pragma table (s408: "pragma tables = language data").
  2. The breaking case to probe: a package that DEFINES `sub import` and calls
     `import foo, 1` meaning its own sub.  perl decides by whether `import`
     is declared; the existing two-Word branch already assumes it is not, so
     the widening must not make that assumption stronger than perl's.

=== MEASURED, NOT SHIPPED (s473w, 2026-09-09) â both settlements answered ===

THE SHAPE THAT FAILS IS NARROWER THAN THE TITLE SAYS.  `import PACKAGE LIST;`
already works when PACKAGE is DECLARED IN THE FILE â probed:

    package My::Mod;  sub import { my $c = shift; print "imported: @_\n" }
    package main;
    BEGIN { $INC{'My/Mod.pm'} = 1; require My::Mod; import My::Mod A => 1; }

  perl: `imported: A 1`   PCL: `imported: A 1`   (identical)

What fails is a package the file does not declare, where the bareword is
compiled as a function call:

    BEGIN { require constant; import constant HAVE_THREADS => 0; }
  perl: HT=0     PCL: dies "Undefined subroutine &main::constant called"

SETTLEMENT 1 â where `constant->import(NAME => VALUE)` lands.  Probed the
METHOD-CALL spelling directly, which bypasses the parser question entirely:

    BEGIN { require constant; constant->import(TWO => 2); }  print TWO;
  PCL dies: `Undefined subroutine &constant::_CAN_PCS called`

So `require constant` DOES find and transpile perl's own core constant.pm, and
that module is unusable here for one reason: its BEGIN installs three
constants by writing a SCALAR REF into its own stash â

    $constant::{_CAN_PCS} = \$const;          # perl's proto-constant-sub (PCS)
    $constant::{_DOWNGRADE} = \$downgrade;

which is the perl-internals rule "a stash slot holding a scalar ref IS a
constant sub".  PCL has no such rule, so `_CAN_PCS` / `_DOWNGRADE` /
`_CAN_PCS_FOR_ARRAY` are never defined and every `if (_CAN_PCS)` in `import`
dies.  Implementing PCS is not the answer.

  => THE LAYER-CORRECT ANSWER IS A `lib/constant.pm` SHIM (CLAUDE.md 9a;
     "pragma tables are language data", s408).  Two facts measured for it:
       * the mechanism it needs WORKS today â installing a sub into a named
         package at run time from a BEGIN, and calling it as a bareword:
             sub install { my ($pkg,$n,$v)=@_; no strict 'refs';
                           *{"${pkg}::${n}"} = sub () { $v } }
             BEGIN { install('main','FOO',42) }  print FOO;   # 42, both
         and `caller` reports the caller's package correctly;
       * it does NOT collide with the compile-time special case: `constant` is
         in `Pl/Parser.pm`'s specially-handled `use` set, so `use constant`
         never loads a module and keeps its `defconstant` lowering.  The shim
         is reached only by an explicit `require constant` / run-time
         `->import`.
     The shim must cover: NAME => VALUE, the multiple-constant HASH form
     (`use constant { A => 1, B => 2 }`), list constants, and the
     `1.21`-and-later rejection rules only as far as the board needs.

SETTLEMENT 2 â the breaking case, probed: a package that DEFINES `sub import`
and calls it as a plain list operator.

    package Mine; sub import { print "own-import(@_)\n" }
                  sub go { import "foo", 1 }
    package main; Mine::go();
    sub import { print "main-import(@_)\n" }  import "bar", 2;

  perl and PCL both print `own-import(foo 1)` / `main-import(bar 2)` TODAY.
  So the widening must NOT be "a Word after `import` is a package": it must be
  gated on `import` not being CALLABLE here â the #266 classifier
  (`_bareword_callable_here`), which is the same predicate the existing
  `@parts == 2` branch should be asking and currently only assumes.

CONCLUSION: the parser half is small (widen the `@parts == 2` branch to
`@parts >= 2` with the #266 gate and lower to `PKG->import(LIST)`), but ALONE
it moves no board row â Scalar-List-Utils t/dualvar.t would then reach
`constant->import` and die at `_CAN_PCS` instead.  The two halves ship
together, shim first.  Estimated one session, not the <= 1 h a filler gets.
subject: `import PACKAGE LIST;` is not the sugar: `import constant HAVE_THREADS => 0;` compiles the PACKAGE NAME as a function call (`(pl-import (pl-constant …))`) and dies "Undefined subroutine &main::constant" -- only the argument-less two-Word form is special-cased
